text:
kai: CI perf alert — microbench/int8 p95 up ~18% after merge r4671. Build: https://ci.redwood/4671/build. Noticed during nightly perf sweep. @maria @eng-oncall
ci-bot: CI: perf/microbench/int8 FAILED (p95 +18%). Full results: https://ci.redwood/4671/perf-report. Attached flamegraph.
maria: :eyes: Pausing canary rollout for r4671. I skimmed the PR — kernel selector change that prefers zero-copy kernels for quantized tensors when align==false. My hunch: fallback interacts poorly with KV cache path and forces extra copies.
alex: Reproduced locally with staging config (kv_cache=true). Profiling shows big memcpy in the "unpack"/routing path around kernel dispatch. Flamegraph: https://fg.redwood/alex/3429
```
perf record -F 99 -- ./microbench --model=gpt2 --batch 8 --seq 512 --quant int8 --kv-cache
perf report --sort comm,ip
```
jin: Did a quick git bisect. Culprit: commit 4671e2b — it changed the selector to prefer zero-copy when payload.align==false. Checkout that commit -> p95 +22% on my machine. Revert -> back to baseline.
sam: Two options: revert r4671 entirely (fast) or add a guard: if kv_cache_hits > 0 prefer copy-friendly kernel. I'll sketch a hotfix PR for the guard.
maria: Also seeing allocator churn — lots of tiny buffer slices created by the zero-copy fallback, causing more GC pauses. Given canary health, let's revert the selector tweak in prod for now. @deploy-bot hold further canaries.
deploy-bot: Deploy paused for canary cluster c-05 by @maria. Reason: perf regression detected in microbench/int8.
alex: I'll add a regression test to CI matrix: microbench with kv_cache=true + quant=int8 and a perf alert threshold. Opened #4680 with the test and perf baseline.
kai: Thanks — after the selector revert patch landed to canary branch tail latency dropped back to baseline. Closing bisect; follow-up: design a zero-copy heuristic that is KV-aware (and avoid small-allocation paths). Will track in an RFC. :thumbsup:
